heroHeadline: Day 9,007 — Op Ghazab Marks Day 100; Taliban: 'Pakistan Will Not Dare Attack' as Russia Military Pact Commences; UNAMA Mandate Expires June 17; Jawid Niazi Day 30; 31-Day Strike Pause
heroSubtitle: June 5, 2026 is Day 9,007 since the US launched Operation Enduring Freedom and marks the 100th day of Pakistan's Operation Ghazab lil-Haq — with all three of Islamabad's core demands (Taliban designates TTP as terrorist, dismantles TTP infrastructure, provides verifiable proof) unmet. No confirmed cross-border Pakistani airstrikes for a 31st consecutive day since the May 5 Dangam (Kunar) strike. Taliban Defense Minister Mohammad Yaqoob Mujahid declared 'Pakistan will not dare execute military attacks inside Afghan territories' and confirmed the Russia-Taliban Military-Technical Cooperation Agreement implementation commences 'within the next few days' — covering repair of Russian-made weapons systems and air defense development. Pakistan dismissed the Russia-Taliban military deal as insufficient to prevent Pakistani air operations. UNAMA's Security Council mandate (extended March 16 for only 3 months) expires June 17 — a renewal vote is imminent as Russia's new Taliban military partnership complicates Council dynamics. Paigard News Agency director Jawid Niazi enters Day 30 in Taliban GDI custody — no bail, no charges, no legal access. Pakistan Defense Minister Asif rejected Taliban Supreme Leader Akhundzada's informal TTP warning as 'insufficient,' demanding verifiable action. Eid al-Adha fell on May 27 and the TTP's 3-day ceasefire (May 27-29) has concluded with no major new attacks.
